# Promoted to repo memory: commit-attribution

Cite these in .sofar/repo.md by qualified handle — `commit-attribution M<n>` —
which is how `sofar doctor` sees that a promoted fact reached repo memory.

- **M1** (2026-08-13T08:02:19.961Z) — `sofar new <slug>` binds the current branch by default, silently replacing whatever binding that branch already had. On a repo like this one — where main carries a live initiative and several sessions share the worktree — that knocks the in-flight initiative off the branch peer sessions and hooks resolve through, with no warning. Check `.sofar/bindings.json` before running it; pass `--no-bind` when the current branch is already bound to live work, then reach the new record with `sofar switch <slug>` or a dedicated branch.
- **M2** (2026-08-13T08:12:05.394Z) — Trailer probe results, git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155), run 2026-08-13 before D4 was taken. Read incantation: `git log --format='%h|%(trailers:key=Sofar-Initiative,valueonly,separator=%x2C)'`. Always pass `separator=` — bare `valueonly` emits a TRAILING NEWLINE that corrupts any line-oriented parse.

Survival: cherry-pick PRESERVES the trailer; rebase PRESERVES it (rebase is a cherry-pick sequence); a commit with no trailer reads back as an empty field, never as a guess.

KNOWN LOSSY PATH — squash merge. `git merge --squash` writes SQUASH_MSG with each original message INDENTED BY FOUR SPACES, so git's trailer parser does not see it and the squashed commit reads back as empty. Committing with `-m` discards SQUASH_MSG entirely and loses it the same way. The slug text is still present verbatim in the body, so a fallback that scans the body for an indented marker recovers it exactly — still reading git, not guessing. Consequence if unhandled: a squash-merged initiative reads as "not shipped" when it did ship — a FALSE NEGATIVE, which is the safe direction but still wrong. Not an issue while this repo commits straight to main; it becomes one the first time work lands through a squashed PR.
